finding: The engraved meridians are NOT parallel: one degree of longitude spans 972.5 px on the top border and 1058.8 px on the bottom, and the six meridians extended meet at latitude ~91.5 deg, i.e. at the pole within engraving tolerance. The plate is a converging-meridian (conic / trapezoidal) construction, not a plate carree.
consequence: MAPGEN-018 fitted an affine to a grid reconstructed from the TOP border alone, so it imposed the top-border x-scale over the whole sheet. That alone produces an east-west error growing southward of roughly 4 percent of the distance from the sheet centre - about 9 km at the corners - which is the systematic pattern MAPGEN-018R measured. The diagnostic explains the failure; it does not repair it, and these ticks are still not two-dimensional control points.
interior_graticule_note: checked at native resolution over open sea and open land; the plate carries graduated borders only, so no interior intersection can be observed and none was interpolated
